answers.a: Lysis of red blood cells by antibodies
answers.b: Clumping of red blood cells by viral surface proteins or lectins

explanations.a: Lysis of red blood cells is hemolyis, not hemagglutination.
explanations.b: Clumping of red blood cells by viral surface proteins or lectins.
explanations.c: Opsonisation is coating of foreign particles to mark them for phagocytosis.
explanations.d: Agglutination of white blood cells is leukoagglutination.

questions.question: Which virus is classically used as the model antigen in HI assays?

explanations.a: HIV is diagnosed primarily via ELISA and Western Blot, not HI assay.
explanations.c: Hepatitis B is detected via serological HBsAg assays, not HI.
explanations.d: Rabies is diagnosed via direct fluorescent antibody tests.

questions.question: What does the HI titer represent?

answers.b: Highest serum dilution that completely inhibits hemagglutination
answers.c: Lowest serum dilution causing complete lysis
answers.d: Number of RBCs agglutinated per mL

explanations.a: Titer measures antibodies, not antigen concentration directly.
explanations.b: Highest serum dilution that completely inhibits hemagglutination.
explanations.c: The assay is based on agglutination inhibition, not cell lysis.
explanations.d: RBC count is not measured by dilution titer values.

questions.question: A positive result (inhibition) in the HI assay indicates:

explanations.a: Absence of antibodies results in hemagglutination (negative HI).
explanations.c: No hemolysis occurs in standard HI assays.
explanations.d: Positive result indicates specific antibody-mediated inhibition, not non-specific clumping.

questions.question: What happens when agglutination is NOT inhibited?

answers.a: RBCs form a button pellet at the bottom
answers.b: RBCs form a diffuse mat/lattice pattern across the well

explanations.a: RBCs form a button when agglutination IS inhibited.
explanations.b: RBCs form a diffuse mat/lattice pattern across the well.
explanations.c: Lysis is not a standard feature of the assay.
explanations.d: Lack of inhibition produces a visible diffuse red film.

questions.question: What is the standard number of haemagglutination units (HAU) per well in HI test?

explanations.a: 1 HAU is too low and reduces test robustness.
explanations.c: 8 HAU increases false negatives by overwhelming the antibodies.
explanations.d: 16 HAU is too high to achieve standard sensitivity.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the principle behind the HI assay?

answers.b: Antibodies block viral HA from binding sialic acid on RBCs, preventing agglutination
answers.c: Complement activation leads to RBC lysis
answers.d: Viral neuraminidase cleaves RBC surface receptors

explanations.a: HI is cell-free and does not involve lysing virus-infected host cells.
explanations.b: Antibodies block viral HA from binding sialic acid on RBCs, preventing agglutination.
explanations.c: No complement is added to the assay mixture.
explanations.d: Neuraminidase cleavage happens but is not the basis of antibody-mediated inhibition.

questions.question: Which of the following incubation conditions is typically used after adding serum and virus antigen together before adding RBCs in the HI assay?

explanations.a: 37°C is sometimes used, but room temperature or 4°C is the standard for pre-incubation.
explanations.b: 56°C is used to heat-inactivate complement in serum, not for virus-antibody incubation.
explanations.d: Freezing prevents binding interactions from occurring properly.

questions.question: The HI assay is performed in which type of laboratory plate?

explanations.a: Flat-bottom plates do not allow non-agglutinated RBCs to settle into a tight button.
explanations.c: Petri dishes are used for cell culture agar plates.
explanations.d: Tube racks do not have microwells for optical reading.

questions.question: Which viral surface protein is targeted in the haemagglutination inhibition assay?

explanations.a: Neuraminidase is targeted in neuraminidase inhibition assays.
explanations.b: Matrix protein is internal and does not bind RBCs.
explanations.d: Nucleoprotein is internal and does not bind RBC sialic acid receptors.
